campaigns.title: Oil Consumption Inspection (Customer Satisfaction Notification)
campaigns.summary: 2015-2018 Jeep Renegade (FWD), 2016-2018 Fiat 500X, and 2015-2018 Ram ProMaster City with the 2.4L engine (sales codes ED6/ED8/EDD/EDE) may exhibit excessive oil consumption from low-tension piston rings, which can eventually cause a stall if unaddressed. The dealer procedure: top off oil, drive a monitored 1500-1700 miles, recheck the level after a 5-minute hot shutdown on level ground. Below the ADD mark = failed test -> long-block engine replacement.
campaigns.reference: NHTSA TSB doc MC-10220586-9999 (Customer Satisfaction Notification W80)
steps: Top off oil to the full mark
Recheck level after a 5-minute hot shutdown on level ground
Below the ADD mark = failed test → long-block engine replacement

campaigns.title: Emissions Recall — Catalyst Efficiency
campaigns.summary: Reported to affect 2015-2016 Jeep Renegade (and other FCA 2.4L Tigershark platform vehicles) with the 2.4L engine: the catalytic converter can lose CO/NOx conversion efficiency after operating at sustained high temperature, causing the vehicle to exceed tailpipe emission standards. FCA's remedy replaces the catalytic converter and reprograms the PCM and TCM with updated software.
campaigns.reference: FCA Emissions Recall U90 — corroborated across multiple independent secondary sources (CarComplaints.com TSB archive, owner/dealer forum postings referencing FCA document numbers MC-10229778-9999 / MC-10226018-9999 / MC-10236888-9999) during a 2026-09 web search; the primary NHTSA/FCA PDF could not be fetched directly in this environment (nhtsa.gov is network-egress-blocked here). Verify exact wording and VIN applicability at nhtsa.gov/recalls or with a dealer before treating this as authoritative.
steps: Confirm a catalyst-efficiency DTC (e.g. P0420/P0430) and/or a failed Mode 06 catalyst monitor
Check FCA campaign U90 applicability by VIN (dealer or nhtsa.gov/recalls)
Dealer remedy: replace the catalytic converter
Dealer remedy: reprogram the PCM and TCM with the latest software
Verify the catalyst monitor passes after a completed drive cycle

campaigns.title: PCM Reprogramming for Oil Consumption
campaigns.summary: A related Customer Satisfaction Notification issuing a PCM software update aimed at oil-consumption behavior on the same 2.4L engine family.
campaigns.reference: Customer Satisfaction Notification W84 (owner-reported; verify applicability by VIN with a dealer)
steps: Verify VIN applicability with a dealer
Apply the PCM software update for oil-consumption behavior when applicable

tsbs.title: MultiAir Actuator Assembly Diagnostic Procedure (2.4L Tigershark Only)
tsbs.summary: When diagnosing P-codes related to the MultiAir unit, the required check order is: (1) verify engine oil is not low, (2) verify the oil filter meets OEM spec, (3) verify oil is not dirty/deteriorated, (4) verify correct oil viscosity/weight, (5) verify oil is not contaminated (coolant/fuel), (6) verify the oil galley screen/filter feeding the MultiAir unit is not clogged — BEFORE replacing the MultiAir actuator itself.
steps: Verify engine oil is not low
Verify the oil filter meets OEM spec
Verify the oil galley screen/filter feeding the MultiAir unit is not clogged
Only then consider MultiAir actuator replacement
